keywords: choice-based conjoint analysis, dual response, stated preference elicitation, discrete choice methods, ordered choice, outside good

abstract: |
  In choice-based conjoint studies, respondents often first pick their preferred product and then state whether they would actually buy it, a design known as the dual-response format. We provide a behavioral foundation for this format and extend the follow-up purchase question from a yes/no answer to an ordinal scale (e.g., "definitely not" to "definitely would buy"). In our model, consumers identify their most-preferred option among a set of alternatives but face uncertainty in their evaluation of the outside good. We develop estimation routines for both aggregate and hierarchical Bayesian versions of the model and apply them to a conjoint study conducted with a consumer insights consultancy. We quantify the information content of the ordinal follow up and demonstrate that it outperforms two common alternatives: collapsing the ordinal scale into a binary response, and assigning a fixed purchase probability to each scale point.
  
bibliography: references.bib
